title: Cross-Functional Lead Retrospective Bulletin — 2027-04-30
content:
Meeting: Cross-functional engineering leadership weekly — serving-runtime focus
Date: 2027-04-30 10:00-11:00 PT (30m focused + 30m deep-dive optional)
Facilitator: Avery Chen
Attendees: Riley Patel, Morgan Blake, Samira Khan, Diego Alvarez, Priya Menon (observability), Jon Park (platform-eng), Maia Rossi (sre - partial)
Summary (TL;DR):
- Short incident last week (partial KV-cache eviction under 512KB load pattern) caused p95 spikes ~400ms for 12m; mitigated via autoscaler bump and quick config rollback.
- Decided to proceed with staged rollout of KV-cache ceiling change (opt-in per-customer) rather than global flip.
- Action items assigned for root-cause follow-up, improved alerting, and one small perf microbenchmark.

Agenda items covered:
1) Incident recap + immediate mitigations (10m)
   - Incident timeframe: 2027-04-26 14:12–14:24 PT.
   - Symptom: sudden increase p95 token-latency on 2 GPU pools handling short-seq chat workloads. No error budget burn but latency SLOs degraded for 12 minutes.
   - Quick fix: bumped autoscaler min-instances + reverted last KV-cache config change rolled earlier that morning (rollback in 5m).
   - Root-cause hypothesis: aggressive KV-cache eviction policy + race in background re-shard when memory watermark reached. (See SRV-1284)

2) Decision log (5m)
   - Decision: Defer global default KV-cache ceiling change. Implement opt-in per-customer config via dedicated feature flag in config service.
   - Rationale: Minimize blast radius for customers on Dedicated while allowing specific low-latency customers to opt in.
   - Owner: Riley (implementation) + Samira (QA gate). Target: canary by 2027-05-10.

3) Observability gaps + alerts (8m)
   - Noted missing dimensionality in latency alert (no pool-level p95 by model_version). Added ticket: SRV-1310.
   - Immediate step: Priya to add temporary dashboard tile showing pool x model p95 for last 90m.
   - Long term: Add adaptive alert thresholds (auto-adjust baselines per pool) — POC in May.

4) Capacity & cost signal (5m)
   - GPU utilization for serving-runtime pools: avg 62% last week, burst to 88% during incident.
   - Recommendation: keep autoscaler headroom config as-is; add a fast-scaling policy for short-burst on chat workloads.
   - Owner: Jon Park to propose policy change by 2027-05-07.

5) Open engineering work + dependencies (optional deep-dive)
   - Feature: Prefix caching improvements (perf bump + memory safety) — PR 472 (code review slow; needs 1 more backend review). Owner: Morgan.
   - Infra: GPU kernel updates planned 2027-05-12 (may require rolling restarts). Coordination: platform-eng + release-eng.
   - Eval: Regression test coverage gap for long-context llama variants — create eval prompt sets. Owner: Samira.

Action items (clear owners + target dates):
- Riley: Implement feature-flagged per-customer KV-cache ceiling; add integration tests. Due 2027-05-06.
- Samira: End-to-end QA plan for KV change + create eval prompt set for long-context. Due 2027-05-08.
- Priya: Add pool x model p95 dashboard tile + temp alert rule. Due 2027-05-02.
- Jon Park: Draft fast-scaling autoscaler policy for chat workloads and review with SRE. Due 2027-05-07.
- Morgan: Get +1 backend review on PR 472 and address review comments. Due 2027-05-04.
- Diego: Postmortem stub (incident timeline + sequence) in Confluence. Due 2027-05-03.

Blockers / Risks / Parking lot:
- Risk: Kernel update on 2027-05-12 could trigger performance variance with quantized kernels; need canary matrix. (Action: release-eng to produce canary plan)
- Blocker: Lack of small-scale repro for eviction race — Diego to reproduce in staging; if cannot, may need targeted tracing instrumentation.
- Parking lot: revisit autoscaler cost-vs-latency tradeoffs at Q2 FY-end review (avoid immediate changes without data)

Metrics snapshot (quick numbers from last 7 days):
- p50 token-latency (hosted chat pool): 24ms
- p95 token-latency (hosted chat pool): 78ms (spike to 480ms during incident window)
- Error rate (5xx): 0.007%
- Avg GPU utilization (primary pools): 62%
- Deployment success rate (canary -> prod): 99.4%

Notes to self / informal capture (explicitly raw):
- "We keep bumping autoscaler headroom — this masks root cause. Need rumble: find low-effort instrumentation to see per-request memory delta in kv cache."
- "Ask infra if the kernel update can be staged on a single AZ first — unblock if they'd prefer global."
- "Follow up with CS: which customers saw the regression? any on Dedicated?" (CS contact: Leah Kim)

Post-meeting quick wins (can do without full tickets):
- Add ephemeral log line in cache manager to emit eviction list size when eviction triggers > 100 items (small PR). Owner: Morgan (target 2d).
- Add short note to release playbook about immediate rollback steps for KV config flips (owner: Diego).

Follow-ups next week (agenda candidates):
- Walkthrough RCA draft + instrumentation plan (Diego + Riley)
- Canary plan for kernel updates (release-eng + platform)
- Cost/latency tradeoff proposal for autoscaler (Jon + product-hosted-api rep)

Attachments / references:
- Incident timeline (stub): https://confluence.redwood/serving-runtime/incidents/2027-04-26
- PR under review: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/472
- Jira: SRV-1284 (eviction race investigation), SRV-1310 (observability alerting)

End notes:
- Overall tone: fast mitigation worked; visibility gap is the bigger problem. We should prioritize light instrumentation and alerting to prevent repeated blasts of autoscaler patches.
- Next meeting: 2027-05-07 10:00 PT (same room) — propose 20m + 20m deep-dive.

---
Raw chat snippets captured during meeting (for context):
- "If we had pool-level p95 per model we'd have spotted the pattern earlier." — Priya
- "Can we make the flag per-customer so CS can toggle for VIPs?" — Riley
- "Kernel update: let's not do a big global rollout until PR 472 merges + we complete a microbenchmark." — Maia

Parking-lot text for follow-on doc: iterate on a lightweight per-request memory probe in staging and ensure no perf cliff for small-batched traffic.

(End of notes)
